analysis.title: US EQUITIES COLOR ON THE WEEK 9 Oct 2026
key_insights: Asset managers finished the week as moderate net sellers while hedge funds were balanced. Macro chop (oil and rate volatility) and anticipation into earnings led to light client activity for most of the week.
Activity picked up Thursday, with a heavy wave of selling in Semis/AI around OpenAI revenue headlines. The selling continued Friday despite a clarification update, and Friday morning snapped back.
The desk describes high-velocity sentiment swings as a feature of the AI investing landscape, contributing to choppy price action and investor performance in recent months.
Long supply appeared in Telcos on the SPCX announcement, and profit-taking appeared in Managed Care after the Medicare STARs results Thursday night.
Prime book: US equities were slightly net sold on the week, with short sales modestly outpacing long buys in single stocks.

Hedge funds rotated into Industrials and out of Info Tech (most notably Thursday), a reversal from the trends seen since the start of September. Health Care saw de-grossing for a 4th consecutive week.
US L/S gross leverage rose 3.8 pts to 213% (53rd percentile one-year). US L/S net leverage rose 0.5 pts to 46.9% (2nd percentile one-year), the first increase in four weeks.
S&P implied move through next Friday (10/16) is 1.06%. CPI is the macro focus, as the last major inflation print before the Fed's October meeting.
Q3 earnings season officially starts with 7% of S&P market cap reporting, beginning with the big banks on Tuesday. Watch headlines from the International AI Summit (Wed) and SEMICON (Tues-Thurs).
Q3 consensus EPS growth is +27% y/y, the highest estimate since 2021, while the median stock is at 9% y/y (vs 14% in Q2).
Last quarter beats were frequent but rewarded with one of the smallest outperformances vs the S&P on record (35bps vs 95bps historically).
Mag7 positioning on the Prime book moved from YTD lows in June (14%) to a record high of 22% of US exposure, after Mag7's most volatile quarter on record in Q2.
